Name: OpenSSH < 9.3p2 Remote Code Execution ( ssh-agent )
Synopsis: The remote SSH server is affected by a remote code execution vulnerability.
Description: The version of OpenSSH installed on the remote host is prior to 9.3p2. It is therefore affected by a remote code execution vulnerability in ssh-agent PKCS#11 provider loading.
Solution: Upgrade to OpenSSH version 9.3p2 or later.

Name: Apache Log4j < 2.15.0 Remote Code Execution (Log4Shell)
Synopsis: Apache Log4j on the remote host is affected by a remote code execution vulnerability.
Description: Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0 JNDI features used in configuration and log messages do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints.
Solution: Upgrade to Apache Log4j 2.17.1 or later.

Name: TLS Version 1.0 and Sweet32 3DES Cipher Suites Supported
Synopsis: The remote service encrypts traffic using deprecated TLS 1.0 and 64-bit block ciphers.
Description: The remote host supports TLSv1.0 and 3DES-CBC cipher suites vulnerable to the Sweet32 birthday attack
Solution: violating FIPS 140-3 and FedRAMP SC-8/SC-13 requirements.
See Also: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 and 3DES ciphers in the web server TLS configuration.

Name: OpenSSH RegreSSHion Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (CVE-2024-6387)
Synopsis: The remote SSH server is vulnerable to a signal handler race condition.
Description: A signal handler race condition in OpenSSH's server (sshd) allows unauthenticated remote code execution as root on glibc-based Linux systems.
Solution: Upgrade OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or apply the vendor security patch.

Name: Apache Commons Text < 1.10.0 StringSubstitutor Interpolation RCE
Synopsis: A Java library on the remote host is vulnerable to variable interpolation RCE.
Description: Apache Commons Text prior to 1.10.0 performs variable interpolation allowing dynamic script execution via dns/url/script lookups.
Solution: Upgrade Apache Commons Text to 1.10.0 or later.

Name: OpenSSH Information Disclosure Discrepancy (CVE-2020-14145)
Synopsis: The remote SSH service has an observable discrepancy during key negotiation.
Description: An observable discrepancy in the SSH handshake allows remote attackers to fingerprint client/server key algorithm state.
Solution: Update OpenSSH or restrict host key algorithms in sshd_config.
